  ## Findings, worst first
  
  ### F1. BLOCKER. The E3 warrants say "no project record states" the link; two project records do
  - **Rows:** BRAIN|A-NOSPEECH|d330, d350, e125, e340 (4).
  - **Claim:** "that aphasia follows stroke is general medical knowledge that no project record states".
  - **Evidence against:**
    - `references/website/data/populations.json` (tracked), Neurological and Acquired Brain Injury profile: "ABI; stroke sequelae (unilateral neglect, navigation impairment, aphasia, hemiplegia)".
    - `governance/functional-taxonomy.md` section 4, NEU row ("FDA term `ABI` resolves here"): maps to "COG-O, AMB, ARO, COM-E". The d330/d350 anchors come from AX-COM-E.
  - **Record cutting the other way, not mentioned:** the same file, line 314, lists "aphasia/dysarthria (COM-E)" as a deferred candidate profile of its own. Filing aphasia under BRAIN is a disposition the taxonomy has not made.
  - **Command:** `grep -rIl -i aphasia --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=transcripts .`
  - **False if:** both passages are absent or not about stroke/ABI.
  
  ### F2. BLOCKER. The COM|A-TIME warrant attributes a quote to the wrong cell and rests on an inference the batch applies inconsistently
  - **Row:** COM|A-TIME|b164.
  - **False fact:** the warrant says `Need A-TIME absorbs: "brain fog impairs organizing time"`. A-TIME's `absorbs` is "slow processing, motor delay, AAC use, screen-reader navigation, translation, distraction". The phrase is in `access_need_icf.notes` for (A-TIME, b164). The script searches absorbs, obligation, notes and map notes, then labels every hit "absorbs". This is the only one of 34 pairs where the hit is outside `absorbs`.
  - **Second false-leaning claim:** "that the identity … carries brain fog is not stated in a project record". Taxonomy section 4 maps `LCOV` to "STA (PEM), THR, COG-O". "Brain fog" is not there verbatim, but a cognitive-demand mapping for long COVID is a record.

  - **Coverage:** this row is the only row for need A-TIME. None of the need's six absorbed terms produced a pair.
  - **False if:** `select absorbs from access_needs where need_code='A-TIME'` contains "brain fog".
  
  ### F3. BLOCKER. 20 warrants append a WHO title from memory to a sentence that begins "governance/functional-taxonomy.md 2.1 lists …"
  - **Shape:** "… lists b210 among the ICF anchors of AX-VIS-N, the seeing-function anchor …". The listing is derived; the gloss is the session's recall, joined by a comma. `base_icf.title` is NULL for each of these codes, and that column exists to make a title from memory impossible.
  - **Rows (20):**
    - BLIND|A-NOSIGHT|b210 ("seeing-function"); DEAF|A-NOSOUND|b230 ("hearing-function")
    - VES|A-STABLE|b235 ("vestibular-function"); VES|A-STABLE|d415 ("posture under visual and motion destabilisation")
    - BRAIN|A-NOSPEECH|d330 ("producing speech"), d350 ("conversation")
    - ADHD|A-LOWLOAD|b140 ("attention-function"); DEM|A-LOWLOAD|b144 and BRAIN|A-LOWLOAD|b144 ("memory-function")
    - COM|A-EFFORT|b455, b130 and MS|A-EFFORT|b455, b130 ("exercise-tolerance", "energy-and-drive"); PAIN|A-EFFORT|b280 ("pain-sensation")
    - AUT, NDV, BRAIN|A-STIMULUS|b156 ("perceptual-function")
    - MH|A-CALM|b152 ("emotional-function"); MH|A-CALM|d240 and AUT|A-CALM|d240 ("stress-handling")
  - **Evidence:** `grep -c -i destabilis governance/functional-taxonomy.md` returns 0. A grep of that file for seeing-function, hearing-function, exercise tolerance, energy and drive, and stress-handling also returns nothing.
  - **Not checkable from the records:** I did not fetch WHO, so whether each gloss is correct is unverified. `v_lens_crosswalk.icf_title` will show the owner a blank beside these rows, so the warrant gloss is the only title they see.
  - **Wider count:** 37 of 135 rows use a NULL-title code (also d230 x7, d310–d329 x2, d330–d349, b117 x4, d166, b435, b440).
  - **False if:** `base_icf.title` is populated for these codes with a `title_source`.
  
  ### F4. BLOCKER (doctrine, for the owner). 23 rows attach a body-function code to an identity, a class of link the project has not held before
  - **Evidence:** `identity_icf_map` holds only d-codes (61 of 61). All b-codes in the batch (rows listed in the closing figures) are new identity-to-impairment links.
  - **Basis offered:** for 21 of the 23, the sole basis is the axis register, whose column header is "ICF anchors (findability)". Section 0.5 clause 2 of the same file, marked binding: "Axes describe specifications, not persons … never a portrait."
  - **Sharpest cases:**
    - DEAF|A-NOSOUND|b230, "the function the need substitutes for". The taxonomy's AX-COM-E row says "Signed languages are languages, not deficits" and section 4 gives DEAF a Deaf-community profile.
    - BLIND|A-NOSIGHT|b210, same phrase.
    - MH|A-CALM|b152; ID, DEM and BRAIN with b117.
  - **False if:** an owner ruling permits b-codes on identities. I found none in `references/project-standards.md`. I did not sweep `sessions/` for it, so this is not a claim of absence there.
  
  ### F5. MUST-AMEND. Every one of the 135 warrants ends with a sentence that review will make false
  - **Claim:** "A proposal for the owner's review, not a determination."
  - **Failure:** `state` moves to `stated` on owner review and the trigger forbids changing `warrant`. A stated row will permanently say it is not one. It also duplicates `state='pending'` (rule 5).

    - "Judged E2 by session_…" duplicates `created_by_session`.
    - The `E1/E2/E3/M` code is defined only in a comment of an uncommitted scratchpad script. No row or schema object decodes it.

    - Warrants copy `mapping_confidence`, `mechanism` and `access_need_icf.notes` verbatim. Those cells can change or be retired; the copy cannot.
  
  ### F6. MUST-AMEND. 13 of the 32 E1 rows do not meet the script's own definition of E1
  - **Definition (script comment):** "the identity's own description names the need".
  - **Do meet it:** VES, MOVE, LPA, TALL, BAR (their descriptions name A-STABLE, A-PRECISION, A-SIZE).
  - **Do not:**
    - DEAFBLIND|A-TACTILE (3 rows): the description says "centring touch".
    - COM|A-EFFORT (6): the description lists conditions only.
    - EPI|A-TRIGGER (1): "photosensitivity is a relevant subtype".
    - COM|A-TRIGGER (3): "MCAS".

  - **Truth:** links 55 and 56 carry "Sensory — partial vision, contrast, lighting dependency", not "spatial orientation, information access". Links 58 and 59 carry "Fatigue + autonomic — exertion limits", not "Autonomic — activity tolerance, exertion limits, thermal".
  - **Command:** `select link_id, mechanism from identity_icf_map where link_id in (41,55,42,56,43,58,44,59)`.
  
  ### F8. MUST-AMEND. 78 of 135 rows carry no three-way judgment
  - **Shape:** support = "need map". The code-level sentence is "access_need_icf holds N -> code (confirmed)" and is identical for every identity paired with that need. The row is the pair crossed with the need's own rows.
  - **e150:** 28 rows, every one of this shape.
  - **Identities whose entire presence is need-side environmental codes:** LPA, TALL, BAR (4 identical rows each), DEAFBLIND (3), EPI (1). That is 16 rows.

  The script accepts any code in either map and never asks that it meet the other side.

  - NDV|A-STIMULUS (5): byte-for-byte the same code set as AUT|A-STIMULUS. NDV's description is "includes AUT, ADHD, and others" and `parent_code` is NULL for all identities, so the batch stores the same judgment under parent and child with no record that it did.

  - **SCI|A-REACH.** Links 26 (d465), 23 (d420) and 24 (d450) are the same codes used for MOB|A-REACH. Section 4 maps SCI to "WHM, REA". The description says "paraplegia or tetraplegia".

    out, status = {}, {}

                                  [r["mechanism"] for (ii, _), rs in imap.items() if ii == I for r in rs]))

            seen.add((I, N, code))
            in_i, in_n = (I, code) in imap, (N, code) in nmap
            if code in common:
                dropped.append(f"{I}|{N}|{code} (held by {len(held[code])} of {nneeds} needs)"); continue
            if code[0] in "db" and in_n and not in_i and (I, N, code) and not tie and code[0] == "d":
                pass
            parts = []
            if in_n and code[0] in "db" and not in_i and code[0] == "d":
                dropped.append(f"{I}|{N}|{code} (need-map activity code; the identity's map does not hold it)"); continue
            if in_n:
                r = nmap[(N, code)]
                parts.append(f"access_need_icf holds {N} -> {code}" + (f" (annotated: {r['notes']})" if r["notes"] else ""))
            if in_i:
                parts.append("identity_icf_map link " + "/".join(str(r["link_id"]) for r in imap[(I, code)]) + f" holds it for {I}")
            if axis:
                if code not in ax.get(axis, set()):
                    errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: {axis} does not list {code} among its ICF anchors"); continue
                parts.append(f"{axis} (status {axstat[axis]}) lists it among its ICF anchors in governance/functional-taxonomy.md 2.1")
            if not in_n:
                if not tie: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: not held by the need's map, so it needs a stated tie"); continue
                if not (in_i or axis): errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: neither map nor anchor holds it"); continue
                parts.append("tie: " + tie)
            title = icf[code]["title"] if icf[code]["title_source"] and "skills/" in (icf[code]["title_source"] or "") else None
            head = f"Code {code}" + (f" (title recorded in base_icf: \"{title}\")" if title else "")
            warrant = f"{p['why']} Need {N} registry text: \"{p['qn']}\". Identity {I}: \"{p['qi']}\". {head}: " + "; ".join(parts) + "."
            row = dict(identity=I, need=N, icf=code, warrant=warrant,
                       support=("both maps" if in_i and in_n else "identity map" if in_i else "need map" if in_n else "taxonomy anchor"))
            (withheld if code[0] == "b" else triples).append(row)

def anchors():
    out, status = {}, {}
    for ln in (ROOT / "governance/functional-taxonomy.md").read_text().splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"\|\s*`(AX-[A-Z-]+)`\s*\|[^|]*\|([^|]*)\|([^|]*)\|\s*([A-Z]+)\s*\|", ln)
        if m:
            out[m.group(1)] = set(re.findall(r"\b[bde]\d{3,4}\b", m.group(2)))
            status[m.group(1)] = m.group(4)
    return out, status

    c = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{ROOT}/data/guidebook.db?mode=ro", uri=True)
    c.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    ax, axstat = anchors()
    idn = {r["identity_code"]: r for r in c.execute("select * from base_taxonomy_identity where status='active'")}
    need = {r["need_code"]: r for r in c.execute("select * from access_needs")}
    icf = {r["icf_code"]: r for r in c.execute("select * from base_icf")}
    imap, nmap = {}, {}
    for r in c.execute("select * from identity_icf_map where retired_at is null order by link_id"):
        imap.setdefault((r["identity_code"], r["icf_code"]), []).append(r)
    for r in c.execute("select * from access_need_icf"):
        nmap[(r["need_code"], r["icf_code"])] = r
    nneeds = c.execute("select count(*) from access_needs").fetchone()[0]
    held = {}
    for (n, code) in nmap: held.setdefault(code, set()).add(n)
    common = {code for code, ns in held.items() if len(ns) * 2 > nneeds}
    errors, triples, withheld, dropped, seen = [], [], [], [], set()
    for p in PAIRS:
        I, N = p["i"], p["n"]
        if I not in idn: errors.append(f"{I}: not an active identity"); continue
        if N not in need: errors.append(f"{N}: not a need"); continue
        ntext = " | ".join(filter(None, [need[N]["absorbs"], need[N]["design_obligation"], need[N]["notes"]] +
                                  [r["notes"] for (nn, _), r in nmap.items() if nn == N]))
        itext = " | ".join(filter(None, [idn[I]["display_name"], idn[I]["description"]] +
                                  [r["mechanism"] for (ii, _), rs in imap.items() if ii == I for r in rs]))
        if p["qn"] not in ntext: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}: need quote not found in the need's records: {p['qn']!r}")
        if p["qi"] not in itext: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}: identity quote not found in the identity's records: {p['qi']!r}")
        for path, sub in p.get("rec", []):
            if sub not in (ROOT / path).read_text(): errors.append(f"{I}x{N}: record {path} lacks {sub!r}")
        for code, axis, tie in p["codes"]:
            if code not in icf: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: code not in base_icf"); continue
            if (I, N, code) in seen: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: listed twice"); continue
            seen.add((I, N, code))
            in_i, in_n = (I, code) in imap, (N, code) in nmap
            if code in common:
                dropped.append(f"{I}|{N}|{code} (held by {len(held[code])} of {nneeds} needs)"); continue
            if code[0] in "db" and in_n and not in_i and (I, N, code) and not tie and code[0] == "d":
                pass
            parts = []
            if in_n and code[0] in "db" and not in_i and code[0] == "d":
                dropped.append(f"{I}|{N}|{code} (need-map activity code; the identity's map does not hold it)"); continue
            if in_n:
                r = nmap[(N, code)]
                parts.append(f"access_need_icf holds {N} -> {code}" + (f" (annotated: {r['notes']})" if r["notes"] else ""))
            if in_i:
                parts.append("identity_icf_map link " + "/".join(str(r["link_id"]) for r in imap[(I, code)]) + f" holds it for {I}")
            if axis:
                if code not in ax.get(axis, set()):
                    errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: {axis} does not list {code} among its ICF anchors"); continue
                parts.append(f"{axis} (status {axstat[axis]}) lists it among its ICF anchors in governance/functional-taxonomy.md 2.1")
            if not in_n:
                if not tie: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: not held by the need's map, so it needs a stated tie"); continue
                if not (in_i or axis): errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: neither map nor anchor holds it"); continue
                parts.append("tie: " + tie)
            title = icf[code]["title"] if icf[code]["title_source"] and "skills/" in (icf[code]["title_source"] or "") else None
            head = f"Code {code}" + (f" (title recorded in base_icf: \"{title}\")" if title else "")
            warrant = f"{p['why']} Need {N} registry text: \"{p['qn']}\". Identity {I}: \"{p['qi']}\". {head}: " + "; ".join(parts) + "."
            row = dict(identity=I, need=N, icf=code, warrant=warrant,
                       support=("both maps" if in_i and in_n else "identity map" if in_i else "need map" if in_n else "taxonomy anchor"))
            (withheld if code[0] == "b" else triples).append(row)
    if errors:
        print("REFUSED:"); [print(" ", e) for e in errors]; sys.exit(1)
    OUT.write_text(json.dumps(triples, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
    OUTW.write_text(json.dumps(withheld, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
    from collections import Counter
    print(f"proposed: {len(triples)}  withheld (b-codes): {len(withheld)}  pairs: {len(PAIRS)}")
    print("dropped:", len(dropped)); [print("  ", d) for d in dropped]
    print("by support:", dict(Counter(t["support"] for t in triples)))
    print("identities proposed:", sorted({t['identity'] for t in triples}))
    print("needs proposed:", sorted({t['need'] for t in triples}))
    print("max warrant length:", max(len(t["warrant"]) for t in triples))

main()

def dispose_adversarial_finding(finding_id: int, disposition: str, ref: str, session: str,
                                reason: str = None, dry_run: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Set a finding's disposition (RC4). Disposition resolves a CONFIRMED defect, so it
    applies only to a SUSTAINED finding, and only once -- a second call is refused rather
    than silently overwriting the first judge's record (CLAUDE.md rule 8: name who judged
    it, permanently, not whoever called last).

    REPAIRED requires `ref` to be an existing data migration path under
    scripts/migrations/. OWNER-RULED requires `ref` of the form
    `references/project-standards.md :: "<verbatim quote>"`, the quote occurring
    exactly once in the ledger's SUBSTANTIVE prose under the RC3 normalisation
    (`dbcore.count_ledger_quote`, excluding SUPERSEDES/BY citation lines) -- the same
    anchor the SUPERSEDES/BY grammar uses. REJECTED and PROVISIONAL-DISPUTED require
    --reason.
    """
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT finding_id, verdict, disposition FROM adversarial_findings "
            "WHERE finding_id=?", [finding_id]).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise Refusal(f"finding {finding_id}: no such finding.")
        if row["verdict"] != "SUSTAINED":
            raise Refusal(
                f"finding {finding_id}: verdict is {row['verdict']!r}, not SUSTAINED. "
                f"Disposition resolves a confirmed defect; nothing to dispose here.")
        if row["disposition"] is not None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"finding {finding_id}: already disposed as {row['disposition']!r}. "
                f"A disposition is not amended by a second call: read the recorded one with SELECT "
                f"disposition FROM adversarial_findings WHERE finding_id = {finding_id!r}, and "
                f"record any correction in the pull request.")
        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "adversarial_findings", "disposition", disposition,
                              f"finding {finding_id}")
        if disposition == "REPAIRED":
            import migrate_db
            valid = bool(
                ref and ref.startswith("scripts/migrations/")
                and migrate_db.DATA_PATTERN.match(Path(ref).name)
                and (dbcore.REPO_ROOT / ref).exists())
            if not valid:
                raise Refusal(
                    f"finding {finding_id}: disposition=REPAIRED requires --ref to be an "
                    f"existing file under scripts/migrations/ matching "
                    f"migrate_db.DATA_PATTERN; got {ref!r}.")
        elif disposition == "OWNER-RULED":
            m = dbcore.LEDGER_REF_RE.match(ref or "")
            if not m:
                raise Refusal(
                    f"finding {finding_id}: disposition=OWNER-RULED requires --ref of the "
                    f"form 'references/project-standards.md :: \"<verbatim quote>\"'.")
            dbcore.require_ledger_quote_once(m.group(1), f"finding {finding_id}: the quote")

  ---
  
  ## Blockers: rulings already made that the migration writes against
  
  ### B1. Warrants rest on the axes layer, which the owner retired

  - **Rulings:**

  - **What a reader takes:** "AX-VIS-N (status ESTABLISHED)" reads as a live, ratified object. This is the F13 repair, and it presents a dropped layer's status as current.
  - **No gate sees it:** `scripts/audit/retired_vocabulary_audit.py` exempts `scripts/migrations/` and `.db` files (lines 29 and 77 of that script).

  - **False if:** a later owner ruling restored axes as a citable basis. `git grep` over the ledger headings and for "axis" found none.
  
  ### B2. MOVE and VES are keyed as identities; the owner ruled they are access needs
  - **Rows (4):** MOVE|A-PRECISION|d440, MOVE|A-PRECISION|e115, VES|A-STABLE|d415, VES|A-STABLE|e240.

  - **Rows (9):** SCI|A-REACH|d465, d420, d450, e120, e155; SCI|A-SELFCARE|d510, d530, e115, e340.
  - **Rulings:**
    - `references/project-standards.md:6111` (seventh set): SCI is "basically" the same population as wheelchair users, "each pair is one population under two names", "a population is held under one code", "do not fan out a grade".
    - Eighth set ACTION (1): "Hold `SCI` and `WHEEL` as one population under `WHEEL`."
    - `:7713-7728` and OI-77: whether SCI is retired is an open owner question. No warrant mentions it.
  - **Duplication:** the SCI code sets equal MOB's exactly for both needs. This is F10's NDV/AUT duplicate rebuilt as SCI/MOB.

Those words belong to MOB's mechanism; the ties were pasted from the MOB pair. Command: `select link_id, mechanism from identity_icf_map where link_id in (23,24,26)`.
  - **SCI|A-REACH|d450 (Walking):**
    - Its tie quotes need text ("ambulatory wheelchair and cane/crutch users") that the SCI warrant's own need quote ("wheelchair users") does not contain.
    - Section 4 gives SCI "WHM, REA, THR, CNT, PAI", with no ambulation.

**RULE: "Axis" is descriptive vocabulary, not a domain identifier.**
The word is ordinary English for how something is arranged, and it must stay freely available for
that. **Precisely for that reason it may not name a specific vocabulary layer.** Overloading it costs
twice: the layer stops saying what it is, and the word stops being usable for plain description.

The layer currently called `axes` carries `icf_b_anchors` and `icf_d_anchors` — it holds
**ICF-anchored access needs**, and must be named for that. Pull a frame as **ICF codes with names**,
never as bare codes: a bare `axis_code` pull once framed four of five searches on `AX-AUD` alone and
hid that the slug also spanned `AX-SPR` (`sessions/session_2026-08-19-research-batch-01-room-acoustic-performance.md` §1(a)).

The entry "Owner instruction 2026-11-16 — the medical taxonomy, the medical maps and the medical codes are deleted" is not edited; it listed five things it supersedes and missed these.

1. **"Owner clarification 2026-11-12 (seventh set) — SCI is basically WHEEL and LMB is basically PROSTH"**, ACTION (4): "Keep impairment level in the medical lens and ICF codes." Superseded as to the medical lens; the clause now reads "keep impairment level in ICF codes", where an ICF body-function code holds the function an injury changes and not the injury.

 dict(i="BRAIN", n="A-PLAIN", qn="brain injury", qi="acquired brain injury",

      ground={"d465": "wheelchair", "d450": "ambul"}),
 dict(i="LMB", n="A-REACH", qn="limb difference", qi="upper-limb disabilities",
      why="The need's registry text names limb difference, and the identity is people with limb differences, upper-limb disabilities.",
      ground={"d440": "hand", "d445": "hand"},
      skip={"e120": "mobility products and technology; the owner placed this identity outside the mobility family (ledger, eighth set)"}),

def main():
    c = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{ROOT}/data/guidebook.db?mode=ro", uri=True)
    c.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    idn = {r["identity_code"]: r for r in c.execute("select * from base_taxonomy_identity where status='active'")}
    need = {r["need_code"]: r for r in c.execute("select * from access_needs")}
    icf = {r["icf_code"]: r for r in c.execute("select * from base_icf")}
    imap = {}
    for r in c.execute("select * from identity_icf_map where retired_at is null order by link_id"):
        imap.setdefault((r["identity_code"], r["icf_code"]), []).append(r)
    nmap = {}
    for r in c.execute("select * from access_need_icf order by icf_code"):
        nmap.setdefault(r["need_code"], {})[r["icf_code"]] = r
    errors, triples, withheld, excluded, seen = [], [], [], [], set()
    for p in PAIRS:
        I, N = p["i"], p["n"]
        if I not in idn: errors.append(f"{I}: not an active identity"); continue
        if N not in need: errors.append(f"{N}: not a need"); continue
        ntexts = [need[N]["absorbs"], need[N]["design_obligation"], need[N]["notes"]] + [r["notes"] for r in nmap.get(N, {}).values()]
        ntext = " | ".join(filter(None, ntexts))
        itext = " | ".join(filter(None, [idn[I]["display_name"], idn[I]["description"]]))
        if p["qn"] not in " | ".join(filter(None, [need[N]["absorbs"], need[N]["notes"]] + [r["notes"] for r in nmap.get(N, {}).values()])):

            elif (I, code) in imap: plan.append((code, "both"))
            else: excluded.append(dict(identity=I, need=N, icf=code, reason=f"need-map {code[0]} code that {I}'s own map does not hold"))
        for code, word in ground.items():
            if code not in icf: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: not in base_icf"); continue
            if (I, code) not in imap: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: the identity's map does not hold it"); continue
            if (N, code) in nmap.get(N, {}): errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: the need's map holds it; no ground needed"); continue

            if word.lower() not in ntext.lower(): errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: ground {word!r} not in the need's own text"); continue
            plan.append((code, "ground"))

            withheld.append(dict(identity=I, need=N, icf=code, reason=why))
        for code, kind in plan:
            if (I, N, code) in seen: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: listed twice"); continue
            seen.add((I, N, code))
            ids = "/".join(str(r["link_id"]) for r in imap.get((I, code), []))
            if kind == "need":
                tail = f"Code {code}: access_need_icf holds {N} -> {code}."
            elif kind == "both":
                tail = f"Code {code}: access_need_icf holds {N} -> {code}; identity_icf_map link {ids} holds it for {I}."
            else:
                tail = (f"Code {code}: identity_icf_map link {ids} holds it for {I}; the word \"{ground[code]}\" appears in that "

    nmap = {}
    for r in c.execute("select * from access_need_icf order by icf_code"):

            if word.lower() not in iside: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: ground {word!r} not in the identity side (link mechanism or recorded title)"); continue
            if word.lower() not in ntext.lower(): errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: ground {word!r} not in the need's own text"); continue
            plan.append((code, "ground"))
        for code, why in p.get("withhold", {}).items():
            withheld.append(dict(identity=I, need=N, icf=code, reason=why))
        for code, kind in plan:

    print("by support:", dict(Counter(t["support"] for t in triples)))

    print("needs:", sorted({t['need'] for t in triples}))

Third pass on `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/migrations/data_20261121014704_2026-11-21-identity-need-icf-triples.sql`. Nothing in the repo was written. I applied the migration to a private scratch copy to read its rows: 92 triples, 4 gaps, 1 pass, 14 findings; `foreign_key_check` empty; canonical DB sha256 unchanged (`e40fa4b0…`). Row ids are identity|need|code.

## 1. Rulings the rows write against

**F1 — BLOCKER — the 9 LMB rows are keyed on a code the owner ruled becomes `UPL`.**
- Rows: LMB|A-REACH|e150, e155, d440, d445; LMB|A-SELFCARE|d510, d540, e115, e150, e340.
- Ruling (eighth set, `grep -n -F "LMB should be UPL for upper limb then" references/project-standards.md`): "LMB should be UPL for upper limb then" / "and that doesnt concern mobility". ACTION (2): "Make `LMB` into `UPL` (upper limb), outside the mobility family, by the sanctioned verb with the successor if it is a new code".
- OI-49 (tenth set) confirmed the wording: `UPL` display name "people with upper-limb differences or disabilities", category `general`.
- The batch applied half of this ruling (excluded LMB e120 as "outside the mobility family") and ignored the other half.
- Computed effect: `db._identity_carriers(conn,'LMB')` on the migrated copy returns `identity_icf_map (6), identity_need_icf (9)`. `retire-identity` refuses while a live carrier exists, and the trigger forbids re-keying. Each of the 9 rows can then leave only by `review --decision reject` under an Owner ledger entry naming its TRIPLE id.
- The need quote "limb difference" also covers lower limb, which the ninth set gave to `LLD` (a child of MOB), not to this identity.
- GAP-379 names the registry lag for ALL, MOVE, VES and SCI only. Adjudication M1 "Repaired" is false for this.
- False if: a later owner line keeps `LMB`. `grep -n -w -E "UPL|LMB" references/project-standards.md` after the tenth set finds only the 2026-11-16 correction, which does not.

**F2 — BLOCKER — the 15 MOB rows name groups the owner gave their own codes.**
- Rows: MOB|A-REACH (5), MOB|A-SELFCARE (5), MOB|A-SIZE (5).
- 2026-08-25 ruling, ACTION (1): "Use the two new codes; do not write new `MOB` rows", marked "not to be relitigated". The third set says its own answer "does not by itself say that the 2026-08-25 ruling is withdrawn."
- Fifth set (OD-14): `WHEEL` is "wheelchair users, including ambulatory and part-time wheelchair users"; `WALKAID` is "crutches, canes, frames, rollators"; MOB stays as parent for "a person with a mobility need who uses no aid".
- OD-31 allows "the parent MOB with no child" only for a provision that names no one. All 15 warrants quote `Identity MOB: "wheelchair users"`, and the A-REACH ones quote "wheelchair users, ambulatory wheelchair users, cane/crutch users".
- `WHEEL`, `WALKAID`, `LLD`, `UPL` are absent from `base_taxonomy_identity` (query returns `[]`). The batch withheld SCI, MOVE and VES for exactly this registry lag, but not these rows.
- The family sentence discloses the keying; it does not make it permitted.
- MOB|A-REACH|d450: the tie "ambul" matches only "ambulatory wheelchair users", who are `WHEEL` by OD-14. OI-03 gives `WHEEL` d465, d420, d410, not d450; d450 is `WALKAID`/`LLD`.
- False if: an owner line after 2026-11-13 permits a row naming wheelchair users on the parent.

## 2. False facts

**F3 — MUST-AMEND — COM|A-EFFORT|d450 and d455: "that link's mechanism" is false for one of the two links named.**
- Warrant: "identity_icf_map link 43/58 holds it for COM; the word "fatigue" appears in that link's mechanism…".
- Link 43 (and 44) mechanism is "Autonomic — activity tolerance, exertion limits, thermal": no "fatigue". Only 58 and 59 hold it.
- This is pass-1 finding 196, whose subject key names these two rows. Adjudication F7 and M7 "Repaired" covered only the BLIND links 41/55/42/56.

**F4 — MUST-AMEND — three ground rows rest only on an ICF title, which GAP-379 (4) says never happens.**
- Rows: LMB|A-REACH|d440, LMB|A-REACH|d445 ("hand"), MOB|A-SELFCARE|d530 ("toilet").
- The word is in no link mechanism (links 35, 36, 9); it is only in `base_icf.title`, whose `title_source` is `skills/functional-deficit-auditor_SKILL.md`, not a WHO payload.
- The warrant's "in that link's mechanism or in the code's recorded title" hides which.
- "hand" matches the need only inside "one-handed operation".
- GAP-379 (4), "never on a title", is also untrue for the 3 `both` rows, which rest on no word at all.

**F5 — MUST-AMEND — "the need's own text" is not the need's text in six rows.**
- DEM|A-PLAIN|d460 and DEM|A-LOWLOAD|d460: "wayfinding" is in no `access_needs` cell; it is only in `access_need_icf.notes` on the e150 row.
- COM|A-EFFORT|d450, d455 and PAIN|A-EFFORT|d450, d455: "fatigue" occurs in A-EFFORT only inside "MS fatigue", another identity's condition.

**F6 — MUST-AMEND — sentences in immutable warrants that are false now.**
- BRAIN|A-PLAIN|e150, e155 and BRAIN|A-LOWLOAD|e150: "The named condition is one member of this identity" follows "names brain injury". Brain injury is the identity, not a member.
- MOB|A-SELFCARE (5 rows): "The named group is one member…", but the need quote is "bathing, dressing, toileting, eating" and names no group.

**F7 — MUST-AMEND — adjudication M8 ("no mutable cell is copied") is false; owner-confirmed changes will falsify 24 warrants.**
- All 92 warrants quote `access_needs.absorbs` as "registry text"; the fifth 2026-11-20 entry records `absorbs` as retired in a later task.
- The 15 MOB rows quote "wheelchair users" from `display_name`; the fifth set renames MOB "disabled people with mobility needs".
- The 9 LMB rows say "the identity is people with limb differences, upper-limb disabilities"; OI-49 rewords it.
- The trigger forbids correcting any of them.

**F8 — MUST-AMEND — gap rows state things their own derive commands and records contradict.**
- GAP-378: its derive query returns A-AT, A-PRECISION, A-TIME. The text explains two; A-PRECISION is unexplained.
- GAP-377: "Rows withheld that the project's own records support" lists COM|A-TIME|b164, of which the generator says "not stated in a project record: this pair is an inference".
- GAP-377: the quoted 'held in ICF b-codes' has 0 hits in the ledger (`grep -c "held in ICF b-codes"`); the text is "held in the medical lens and ICF b-codes".
- GAP-379 (2): the "no activity code" query returns BLIND and BRAIN, which hold 8 and 5 live map links. The gap does not say why.
- GAP-380: "attacked by three read-only passes… The later two… are in adjudication.md and the committed transcripts". `adjudication.md` holds pass 1 and 2 only, and the third transcript (`…01-47-16_adversarial_a47c5fca.jsonl`) is untracked. It was written as fact before the pass returned.

**Notes.**
- BRAIN|A-NOSPEECH|e125, e340 cite "populations.json" with no path. The file is `references/website/data/populations.json`, entry `NEU` (a retired code, `last_updated` 2026-04-09), whose profile lumps MS, Parkinson's and epilepsy, now separate identities. The quote itself is present.
- GAP-377 cites `governance/functional-taxonomy.md` by line number (38–41). It is correct today; the sentence there is about axis b-code anchors.

## 3. Overclaim

**F9 — MUST-AMEND — the ground word does not tie the code; it coincides at identity level.**
- 13 of the 16 ground words sit in a mechanism string that is identical on every code of that identity.
- The generator's own test admits 44 further rows inside the judged pairs that were not proposed. Examples:
  - DEAF|A-NOSOUND|d330–d349 ("alert", same string as the proposed d310–d329; in v1, dropped in v3).
  - DEM|A-LOWLOAD|d230 and d710–d729 ("memory", "attention", "wayfinding").
  - AUT, NDV, MH |A-STIMULUS on d710–d729, d910–d920, d570, d910 ("sensory").

- For d230 (AUT, NDV, MH |A-STIMULUS) and d310–d329 (DEAF) `base_icf.title` is NULL, so no record says what the code is. Choosing d230 over the identity's other codes can only come from memory of the ICF title: pass-1 F3 in an unrecorded form.
- The 2026-04-09 rule that an MH room is "distinct from" the sensory quiet room cuts against the MH "sensory" tie.
- False if: a record names why this code and not its siblings.

**F10 — MUST-AMEND — adjudication M7/M9 "no verified shared word" is false for BLIND.**
- "vision" is in the mechanisms of links 55, 56, 57 ("partial vision…") and in A-NOSIGHT `absorbs` ("low vision, colour vision deficiency").
- By the stated rule BLIND|A-NOSIGHT|d310–d329, d460 and d620 pass. BLIND therefore shows as "no activity code" for a reason that is untrue.

**F11 — MUST-AMEND — 73 of 92 rows are the judged pair crossed with `access_need_icf`, and 10 identities have nothing else.**
- e-only identities (rows): ADHD 1, EPI 1, MS 2, DEAFBLIND 3, ID 3, BAR 4, LPA 4, TALL 4, BLIND 4, BRAIN 10.

The 2026-07-24 rule says "TALL is included for fit, not as a disability-identity claim".

**F12 — MUST-AMEND — pairs with no naming on either side are not disclosed as inference.**
- MOB|A-SELFCARE and LMB|A-SELFCARE: the need names activities, not people. The only support is shared d510/d540, and 6 e-rows ride on it.

  * Not paired, and why: A-AT (registry note flags its scope for the owner); ALL (a scope marker, ledger OD-31);
